headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Dify can read/write files and call external APIs while dbt-core touches warehouse data and can be fed into orchestration flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest files and wire tools into agent/workflow apps, so attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions if dbt-core outputs are routed into it. dbt-core itself is not a chat agent, but its warehouse-facing outputs can become content for Dify. The shared path is plausible, though not proven by direct pair evidence.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are copied into a Dify agent prompt or workflow input
IF Dify tools are configured to parse file contents as instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation template
Disable automatic prompting from uploaded files
Review any dbt artifact before passing it into Dify
Use a read-only handoff file format
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between dbt outputs and Dify inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, and Dify can read uploaded knowledge-base files, write files, and send data to model providers and tool APIs. If warehouse outputs or logs are moved into Dify, sensitive data can leave the warehouse boundary through broad egress. The pairwise leakage path is credible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF warehouse extracts or dbt artifacts are uploaded into Dify
IF Dify is connected to a third-party model provider or external tool endpoint
mitigations: Restrict Dify to synthetic or redacted inputs
Block sensitive dbt artifacts from upload
Use a separate Dify tenant for non-sensitive data
Audit outbound model-provider destinations
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on the dbt-to-Dify handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and broad network egress, while dbt-core calls a data warehouse and may be used in the same operational pipeline. Even without modify_git_state, overlapping mutable access to shared artifacts or warehouse-backed outputs can create conflicts in default orchestration setups. Uncertainty about the exact shared resource pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory or artifact store
IF dbt runs concurrently with Dify workflows that mutate shared outputs
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Serialize writes to shared artifacts
Make dbt outputs immutable before Dify reads them
Use per-run filenames with timestamps
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can orchestrate tools and workflows, so dbt-core outputs may be treated as authoritative inputs if passed through without verification. dbt-core can generate warehouse-derived facts, and Dify can then render or act on them. The pair creates a realistic no-check handoff, but not an automatic action chain by default.
conditions: IF Dify consumes dbt-generated tables, docs, or summaries as trusted context
IF no validation step checks dbt output freshness or correctness
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Dify consumes dbt output
Require schema checks on dbt artifacts
Mark dbt-derived content as untrusted in prompts
Limit Dify actions to read-only summaries
requires-engineering: add automated provenance and freshness checks

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while Dify handles conversation logs, knowledge-base files, and model-provider API keys. If regulated data is moved from the warehouse into Dify, retention and residency obligations can diverge across systems. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is uploaded into Dify knowledge-base files or logs
IF Dify retention settings differ from warehouse retention policy
mitigations: Classify data before any dbt-to-Dify transfer
Exclude regulated rows from Dify inputs
Align retention settings across both systems
Document residency for each data flow
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated datasets
